clauses.reason: This clause amends level IV of the parent by changing subsection (10) from Assistant to Counselor. Executive Order 12076, signed 1978-08-18, states "Executive Order No. 11861, as amended, is hereby revoked." and has no delayed effective date. Later event: Executive Order 12060, signed May 15, 1978, section 1 provides for "by deleting “Counselor to the Secretary for Congressional Affairs” in subsection (10)", which replaces the title and is an amendment, so the clause continues until the parent is revoked.

This clause adds item (9) Deputy Assistant Secretary for Housing, Department of Housing and Urban Development, to level V. Section 2 of Executive Order 11976 states that section 2 of the parent, as amended, "is further amended by deleting" that entry; no effective-date sentence appears in the held text, so the date is its signing date, 1977-03-11. Later event: Executive Order 12076 revoked the parent on 1978-08-18, after the entry was gone.

inventory_overrides.reason: Override of the one-clause machine inventory: section 1 and section 2 of the held text are separate operative commands with different ends; this scope covers section 1 in full.
Override of the one-clause machine inventory: this scope covers section 2 (level V item (9) Deputy Assistant Secretary for Housing) in full.

research_rationale:
Identity: the held Federal Register text (41 FR 30583, issue of July 26, 1976) is Executive Order 11927, signed July 22, 1976, which amends Executive Order No. 11861, as amended, in two sections. I read the whole order. Section 1 amends level IV: Section 1 of the parent "is further amended by deleting “Assistant” in subsection (10)" and inserts Counselor in lieu of Assistant. Section 2 amends level V by adding (9) Deputy Assistant Secretary for Housing, Department of Housing and Urban Development. The representation is the machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF. The machine inventory has one clause, but the two sections have different first ends, so I override it with two scopes. Ends: section 2's entry was deleted by Executive Order 11976, section 2, signed March 11, 1977 (42 FR 14081); section 1's change lasted until Executive Order 12076 revoked the parent on August 18, 1978 (43 FR 37161). The whole-order end is the later date, 1978-08-18.

savings.reason: Executive Order 12076 section 1-201 contains the clause beginning "Nothing in this Order shall be deemed to terminate or otherwise", and goes on to protect the appointment of any occupant of a position listed in its section 1-1 who held it immediately before that order, which keeps appointments of holders of the positions it re-lists after the parent was revoked.
